thresholds.opaque: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: a typed-sorts sidecar names "types_fallback": "opaque" (the only value; anything else is refused). Without the key nothing changes: holon types refuses the milestone on an ill-sorted term (exit 2, nothing written), as N2 says. Under the key, holon types types each document of the sidecar on its own, in sorted order. A document whose typed model generation raises the ill-sorted error is OPAQUE: (O1) it is a recorded miss, one entry of gen/<M>/sorts/opaque.json {document, sha256, model, term, reason}, where term is the action and the operation named by the error (its first clause, before ': ') and reason is the error's whole text, which names the operation and its source span; the miss is never silent and the composed row counts it (types_opaque). (O2) Its STATE: it has no typed model, so no state variable of it exists in any model; nothing constrains it. (O3) Its ACTIONS: none is modelled; no law of any rule is derived over it (typed part, DISCH, FACT, UNDO, SORT, SYM), so every claim over it is UNKNOWN (counted at the document: one miss). (O4) What OTHER documents may assume about it: nothing new. Every typed model is one document's: another contract is reached only through an external call, whose answer is a free value (A-env) whether or not the callee is typed, so a typed document's model, laws and verdicts do not depend on whether an opaque document is in the milestone, apart from the milestone-wide assignment hash the model's header comment names (and so its model_sha256). (O5) Every stage after types (model, disch, derive, run) reads the typed documents only: the sidecar's documents minus the opaque ones; the sort pass and types read every document. The sort assignment is the sort pass's over all documents, unchanged. (O6) A taint violation (G4) still refuses the milestone, and an error that is not the ill-sorted one (an unreadable input) still exits 1. (O7) If every document is opaque, holon types writes types.json with no model and exits 0; the later stages then have no document and derive no typed law.
thresholds.soundness: Opacity only removes: an opaque document contributes no model, no state constraint, no action and no law, and it changes no typed document's model (O4). So the set of laws decided under the fallback is a subset of the laws the same milestone would decide without that document, each with the same verdict. No law can be PROVED or REFUTED through an opaque document.

thresholds.search: Part (2), fixed here before any build commit. The search decides, for one affine component, whether the classes' role domains (subsets of {P, G}) admit an assignment satisfying every ternary table (+: (P,G,P) (G,P,P) (G,G,G); -: (P,P,G) (P,G,P) (G,G,G)); with P = 1 and G = 0 each table is 'out = lhs + rhs' or 'lhs = rhs + out' with no carry, a 1-in-3-type relation, so the problem is NP-complete with seeds and exponential in the worst case under any exact strategy. The old strategy (I110) propagates (generalized arc consistency), then branches on the least open variable, chronologically. On a network whose leftover parts are independent, a part that fails is re-discovered under every combination of choices in the parts sorted before it: exponential thrashing. The rewrite, D1: after each propagation, the constraints that hold a variable with more than one role left are grouped by the connected components of those variables; a constraint with every variable decided is satisfied (propagation left it a supporting row) and drops out; with two or more parts, the network is satisfiable iff every part is, each searched on its own (in order of its least open variable, stopping at the first that fails); with one part, the old branching is unchanged. D1 is an evaluation strategy only: _search returns the same boolean on every input, so the satisfiable verdict, every role set (Component.roles), role pair and difference sort, and so every sort output, are the same. Which roles are admissible is never changed. The flag holon.sorts.solve.DECOMPOSE (True; False is the old strategy) exists for the identity test only. No new cutoff and no new tier: the sort budget's tier stays I110's 5,000,000. The units keep I110's definition (one search node, one table row a propagation sweep reads, ...); D1's own scan of a node's constraints is not metered (one pass over the constraints that the same node's propagation reads at least three rows of each, so time stays within a constant factor of the metered work).

thresholds.routing: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: the protocol names run_routing "per_runner". Without it the driver's run step is I110's two calls, unchanged. Under it, holon.eval.holon_run.route(derivation) groups the derived law ids, each by its laws/<M>/DERIVATION.json entry: disch: rule DISCH with a sub-form of holon.disch.run.SUBFORMS; fact: rule FACT; typed: rule SORT with sub-form as_member, realize or reinterpret, and rules UNDO and SYM; milestone: every other law (PAR and every route C family). Each non-empty group is one `holon run --milestone M --laws <ids> --out results/M --gen-dir gen/M` call, in the order disch, fact, typed, milestone, with only its runner's arguments: disch --sidecar <typed> --disch <disch> --section-errors unknown (when the protocol names disch.section_errors); fact --sidecar <typed> --fact-sidecar <fact>; typed --sidecar <typed>; milestone none. A call that fails is recorded (its exit) and the next one runs. A law with no record after every call is UNKNOWN with no record. The stage detail holds aggregates only (per runner: laws, status, exit, records, section errors).
thresholds.section_errors: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: `holon run ... --section-errors unknown` (holon.disch.run). Without it a holon.disch.section.SectionError raised while building one document's DISCH section propagates and stops the runner, as before. Under it, when building a document's section (holon.disch.run.Doc) raises SectionError, that document's section is in error: every DISCH law the run names whose facts document is that document gets a record with status UNKNOWN, kernel verdict not_run, checker not_run, no witness, attempts [{kind: section, error: <the error's text>}] and bound "the DISCH section of <model> is refused: <the error's text>"; no candidate, proof or search is attempted for it, so an error never yields PROVED or REFUTED. Every other document's section is built and its laws decided as before; S3's neighbourhood seeds are taken from the laws of the same document only (unchanged), so another section's error changes no verdict of a section without one. Only SectionError is caught: any other exception still stops the runner.
thresholds.opaque_classes: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit; Q81). Opt-in only: a typed-sorts sidecar under types_fallback "opaque" names types_opaque_classes, a non-empty sorted subset of ["gen_error", "member_layout", "unsupported"]; any other value is refused when the sidecar is read, and the key without types_fallback is refused. Absent, the classes are ["gen_error"] and every output is I111's byte for byte. A document's typed model generation that raises holon.sorts.model3.GenError, whatever the GenError (the lead's correction to Q81, relayed before this prereg: not only I111's ill-sorted case; I111's code already catches every GenError, so this names its class), is class gen_error; holon.machine.MemberLayoutError (a ModelError subclass raised exactly where holon.machine refuses a field whose slot or offset is not the compiler's member layout of its family's type, the refusal I111 recorded; its text is unchanged) is class member_layout; holon.extracted_eval.Unsupported is class unsupported. A document is opaque when its error's class is named; each miss then also records class (only when the sidecar names types_opaque_classes). I111's O2-O7 are unchanged: no model, no state, no action, no law; every later stage reads the typed documents only. A milestone-wide input error stays a refusal of the milestone: the assignment, the sidecar, the seeds or the binding unreadable (exit 1), a taint violation (exit 2), and every other exception, ModelError included (a family's slot or offset not in the compiler's layout at all, a document that cannot be loaded), refuse the milestone as before.

thresholds.unbound: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: holon run ... --unbound unknown (holon.mpipeline's run and holon.codecrun.decide; the composed driver passes it to the milestone runner under protocol run_unbound "unknown"). Without it every output is as before, and a BindingError stops the runner as before. Under it, before a law of the milestone runner is decided, its binding is computed: the kernel cone (holon.bindings.kernel_cone) of the law's statement roots (holon.records.ir_roots_text) over the kernel entries of the model the law is decided over. If that raises holon.bindings.BindingError, nothing is attempted for the law: its record has status UNKNOWN, kernel verdict not_run, checker not_run, no witness, no law or proof file, attempts [{kind: binding, error: <the error's text>}] and bound "not decided: the statement cannot be bound to its model: <the error's text>"; its deps entry has an empty cone. If the cone of the decided statement text (after the decision) raises BindingError, the decision is dropped the same way (status UNKNOWN, its law and proof files removed). Every other law is decided as before. Only BindingError is caught.
thresholds.bind: The definition (fixed here, before any build commit). Opt-in only: protocol bind "derived". After the run step, the composed driver runs holon bind --milestone M --root <scratch root> --unbound skip (stage bind): every derived law is bound by holon.bindings.bind_law, as route A's milestones are, into the scratch root's spec/bindings/<M>.json (written fresh: the scratch root's copy of spec/bindings holds no <M>.json, and nothing is written to the repository's spec/bindings); a law whose bind_law raises BindingError is left out and listed in spec/bindings/<M>.unbound.json {law id: error}. --unbound skip is refused on a milestone whose spec/bindings/<M>.json already exists (an existing binding only changes through the statement lifecycle, unchanged). Then the binding check (holon.eval.holon_run.binding_check): a PROVED or REFUTED record is admitted only when its law is bound and the binding's statement_hash equals the record's statement_hash and the binding's model equals the record's artifacts.model; any other decided record is rewritten UNKNOWN (kernel and checker not_run, witness and difference null, artifacts laws and proof null, attempts + [{kind: binding_check, error}], bound "not decided: the binding check refuses the record: <why>"). An UNKNOWN record is left as it is. No family is exempt: every derived law, whatever its runner, goes through holon bind and the check (G2 binds every law of a milestone: holon.bindings.derive over ir.load_laws_any). The stage's detail holds aggregates only: laws, bound, unbound, decided records refused. The bindings and the unbound list name law ids, so they go to the vault (Q56) and are never copied into the committed output.

thresholds.disch_fallback: The definition (D), fixed here before any build commit. Opt-in only: a DISCH sidecar (holon-disch/0.1) names document_fallback "unknown" (the only accepted value; any other value, or a non-string, is refused when the sidecar is read, exit 2). The composed driver writes it into every DISCH sidecar it generates when the protocol names document_fallback.disch "unknown". Absent, every output of holon disch, derive and holon run is as before, byte for byte. Under it, holon.analysis.closure.Sidecar.analyses, which holon disch, derive's rule DISCH and holon run's DISCH runner all read, analyses each document on its own: a document whose analysis (rules D1-D10) raises holon.analysis.closure.ClassError (class class_error) or a KeyError, TypeError or IndexError (class malformed; before, the refusal 'malformed') falls back. A fallen-back document has no DISCH analysis: no class, closure, basis element or DISCH law is derived over it (its DISCH laws are UNKNOWN: no DISCH claim over it is made, so none is decided), and it is a recorded miss in <out>/fallback.json {document: disch_fallback, milestone, sidecar {path, sha256}, documents: [{document, sha256, model, class, error}]} beside closure.json and conjuncts.json, which list the analysed documents only. fallback.json is written only under the opt-in (holon disch --check compares it too). What a fallen-back document contributes to later stages: nothing to DISCH (no law, no section, no search seed); its typed model, its laws of every other rule family and its evidence are unchanged (the fallback is DISCH's only). What other documents may assume about it: nothing; each document's analysis reads its own document and the sidecar's r0 only (an external call is an A-env unknown), so every other document's analysis, its laws and their records are exactly as without the fallen-back document. Milestone-wide input errors stay refusals of the milestone (exit 2, nothing written): the sidecar missing, not JSON, of another version, without documents, or with an inputs sha256 that does not match; a document missing, not JSON or not a transitions document; two documents naming one model; r0 naming a path a document does not declare; the hypothesis verdicts unreadable. thresholds.evidence_fallback: The definition (E), fixed here before any build commit. Opt-in only: the milestone's adoption sidecar (spec/<M>/lib/derive_extracted.json, holon-derive-extracted/0.1) names document_fallback "unknown" (the only accepted value; any other is an EvidenceError when the set is built). The composed driver adds it, when the protocol names document_fallback.evidence "unknown", to the adoption sidecar holon roles installed for the entry in this run (one that did not exist before roles ran), never to a hand sidecar. Absent, every evidence document is as before, byte for byte. Under it, holon.diagram.evidence.build, for an adopted transitions document whose E2 atoms (holon.diagram.evidence.transitions_atoms, rule Z1-Z3) raise for a construct the rule over transitions documents does not map (holon.diagram.transitions.TransitionsError, class e2_unmapped), keeps the document's model with its anchors (transitions_anchors, unchanged) and gives it no atom: exactly the model a build that reads no committed diagram gives an adopted document (its laws' evidence levels [], the computed default triage). The miss is recorded in the evidence document under fallback: [{document, sha256, model, class, error}], a key written only when a document falls back (so a set with no fallen-back document is byte-identical to one without the opt-in). Derive (holon.rules._committed_par_inputs) rebuilds the evidence set with holon.diagram.evidence.build_milestone over the same adoption sidecar, so it reads the same set and the derive refusal 'the evidence set cannot be rebuilt' for that document falls back with it: that is the per-document derive refusal this key takes down. What a fallen-back document contributes to later stages: its anchors and no atom. Evidence is triage, not a premise: no law's statement, proof or verdict reads an atom of a transitions model (PAR's components take the atoms of their own component model only, and a transitions model is never a PAR component), so a law over the document has the evidence levels [] and every law's claim and verdict is as the checker decides it. What other documents may assume about it: nothing; E2 pairs are pairs of one document's own actions, so every other model's anchors and atoms are byte-identical. Milestone-wide input errors stay refusals: the adoption sidecar, the lexicon, a component document or its diagram missing, malformed or stale; two documents sharing a model name; a component's (codec, Go-op, count or OWN document's) construct the pass cannot map; a transitions document's anchors that cannot be read. thresholds.derive_scope: Derive refusals for one document other than the evidence rebuild (a PAR component's ParError, a typed producer's rule error) are not in this key: they stay refusals of the milestone, and are reported under Not done.

thresholds.soundness: A fallback only removes constraints, never adds them. (D) removes every DISCH claim over the fallen-back document and adds none; no other document's analysis reads it, so no other DISCH law changes; its other laws are derived and decided exactly as without the fallback. (E) removes atoms only, and atoms are triage: no statement, premise or verdict reads a transitions model's atom. So neither fallback can turn a law that would be REFUTED, or that holds only under a constraint of the fallen-back document, into PROVED. Every REFUTED still needs its replay, and on a deployed system follows Q56.

thresholds.definitions: (1) holon.gen.goint (fixed here, before any build commit; each quoted from the Go specification in its docstring). A value of a Go integer type T of n bits is represented by the 64-bit two's complement of its mathematical value (sign-extended for signed T, zero-extended for unsigned), Bend's Word(64n) LSB first; fit(v, T) truncates to n bits and reads them in T's signedness ("Conversions": sign or zero extension, then truncation). int, uint and uintptr are 64 bits (the pinned linux/amd64 toolchain; the differential test checks it). + - * & | ^ &^: the 64-bit result fit to T ("Integer overflow": modulo 2**n). / and %: truncated division (|a| / |b| unsigned, negated when the signs differ; the remainder has the dividend's sign), so MinInt / -1 = MinInt and MinInt % -1 = 0; a zero divisor panics. << and >>: the result has the left operand's type; a count of 64 or more saturates (0, or the sign in every bit for >> of a negative signed value); >> is arithmetic for signed T and logical for unsigned; a count of a signed type whose value is negative panics. Unary -x = 0 - x and ^x = all bits flipped, fit to T. Comparisons order the values: signed order on signed T, unsigned order on unsigned T. Undefined (no definition; the op's laws stay UNKNOWN): any operand that is not of an integer type (float, complex, string, a named type whose underlying type the document does not give), an op outside these.
thresholds.frontend: (2) Opt-in only: the codec frontend's config key ops "typed" (config holon-go-frontend/0.3; any other value refused), passed by the composed driver from protocol go.ops "typed" (never to the Go machine frontend, whose documents are extracted as before). Under it: every path-enumerated function (codec-shaped or not) emits its paths and a typed section {stale, terms: [[term, Go type]] (a term met with two types recorded null), lengths: {param: array length | null}}; the reasoner's linear forms read an op or unop term as one variable (never as an exact linear combination: Go integers wrap); a path that loads a term after a store through memory the enumerator does not model, or after a call (other than len or cap), marks the function stale. Without it every output is as before.
thresholds.class: (3) The straight-line class (holon.gen.gostraight), only for an op whose Go-op entry has the typed section and no loop body. Carrier kinds: bytes (a byte-array parameter of known length n; cell k is byte k; cell map (1, 0, n)) or fields (any other parameter: the leaves are the field paths from the parameter the component's ops read, each two U32 cells (hi, lo) at its place in the component's sorted leaves: an integer field's value is hi*2**32+lo fit to its type, a bool field is lo != 0, a field compared with nil is nil when lo == 0, a field's len is (hi mod 2**31)*2**32+lo; a nil receiver is not a value of the model, rule A-goloop-fields). A path is the conjunction of its atoms, each an integer comparison of terms over the leaves (or a bool field's truth, or a field's nil-ness), its outcome its end (OPanic, OErr, ORet). Unsupported (the op undefined, its laws unbound and UNKNOWN): a term outside the class, a term of no or two recorded types, a division or remainder whose divisor is not a non-zero constant or a shift whose count is a signed non-constant (the frontend's paths record no panic for them), a stale fields op, a continue path, paths that do not partition the sample points. Candidates for a law (as goloop's rule Y7, in this class): per op of the component by model name, the first sample point (lexicographic over the leaves' sample values: 0, 1, 2, the type's extremes, each constant of the op and its neighbours; a seeded subset of 65536 when the product is larger) at which the op's outcome is OPanic, then OErr, then ORet. A law is REFUTED only by a counter-law Bend accepts at a candidate; no proof route (UNKNOWN otherwise, gap G6). The model text of a document with no straight-line op is byte-identical to before.

thresholds.coverage_skip: The definition (C), fixed here before any build commit. holon coverage --typed-only (only with --sidecars, the composed route's form; without --sidecars it is refused, exit 2). Each given extraction sidecar is accounted for exactly as before, unless (i) its output document is not a file under the root (reason not_extracted: the frontend refused it, so there is no document, no model and no law over it), or (ii) its output is listed in the milestone's gen/<M>/sorts/opaque.json documents (reason opaque: I111's O2-O7, no typed model, no state, no action and no law over it). Such a sidecar is not walked; it is listed in the report under skipped [{document, reason}], sorted by document. The key skipped is written only under --typed-only, so a report without it is byte-identical to before. The composed driver passes --typed-only when the protocol names document_fallback.coverage "typed_only". Soundness: holon.records.coverage_field reads a law's own document's entry only, and no law is derived over a skipped document, so no record reads a skipped entry; coverage is reported debt, never a premise. An extracted, typed document whose walk refuses still refuses the stage (not in this key).
thresholds.run_fallback: The definition (R), fixed here before any build commit. Opt-in: the protocol names document_fallback.run "unknown". The composed driver's per-runner step (holon_run._run_routed) runs each runner group as before. When a group's holon run exits non-zero, the group is re-run once per law document (the law's facts, from its laws/<M> file; documents sorted, each with the group's own arguments and --laws its laws over that document). A document whose re-run exits 0 keeps the records it wrote. A document whose re-run exits non-zero falls back: every law of the group over it gets the fallback record, written over any record the failed runs left: status UNKNOWN, scope bounded, bound "not decided: document fallback (run): <error>", no witness, no difference, triage none, kernel verdict and checker not_run, artifacts laws, proof and law_name null, attempts [{kind: document_fallback, stage: run, runner, error}] (error: the re-run's last output line). The failure is not confined to one document, and the group stays a refusal, when the first run or a re-run exits 2 (the runner refused its input), or when there are at least two documents and every re-run fails with the same last output line once every law id (L followed by word characters) and every law document path of the group are masked: then no record of the group is kept (the group's laws have no record, as a refusal writes none) and the runner's row says milestone_refusal true. The row's runner aggregates add fallback_documents and fallback_laws (counts only, Q72: no law id). Absent the opt-in, every output is as before. What a fallen-back document contributes: no decision in that runner; every other runner and every other document's laws are decided as without it. What other documents may assume about it: nothing; each document's re-run reads only its own laws, and the runner decides each law over its own document's model.
thresholds.bind_fallback: The definition (B), fixed here before any build commit. holon bind --unbound document: I115's --unbound skip (a BindingError leaves that law out of spec/bindings/<M>.json and lists it in <M>.unbound.json, refused as skip refuses a milestone that already has a bindings file) plus a per-document fallback: an exception other than BindingError (an Exception, not KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit) raised by bind_law for a law L over document D (L's facts, a string) falls back when no law over another document has L's model (holon.bindings.model_path, computed for every law before binding; a law whose model_path raises is its own model). Then every law over D is left out of <M>.json and listed in <M>.unbound.json with "document fallback: <class>: <message>", and spec/bindings/<M>.fallback.json {milestone, documents: [{document, class, error, laws}]} (sorted) records it; the changes log line names the documents under fallback. Any other failure refuses: a failure before or outside the per-law step (the configuration, loading the laws), L with no facts string, or L's model shared with another document's law: exit 1, nothing written (as before). The composed driver passes --unbound document when the protocol names document_fallback.bind "unknown"; its bind aggregate adds fallback_documents and fallback_laws. Then binding_check (I115, unchanged) refuses every decided record of an unbound law, so every decided record over D is rewritten UNKNOWN. Absent the opt-in, every output is as before.

A family's reason: derived (laws > 0); no_input (an input count is 0: a reported coverage limit, the family covers nothing the target declares); input_no_law (inputs present, no law); part_absent. Every recorded step is 1 or none. S1 is the class of the first shape (Q93 (3): the shape the corpus's ops use most); S2 (constant strides) is defined from the Go specification and has no corpus op; sequential, nested and unbounded loops, calls before reads and conditions over call results stay outside (Q93 (3): they need an inter-procedural model). No entry name, path or identifier appears in a class's definition or its code.
thresholds.definitions: Each class is fixed here, before any build commit, from the Go specification ("For statements with range clause", "For statements with for clause", "Integer overflow", "Index expressions", "Comparison operators"); both are tried only after goloop's I67 class refuses an op (Unsupported), so an op in that class is modelled exactly as before. S1 (range): an op with one parameter p and exactly one loop, the loop_bodies entry's init the constant 0, step 1, cmp <, limit len(X) where X is p or a field path from p (field of field ..., through pointer dereference), X of slice type []E with E an integer type of at most 32 bits, and paths over the symbolic index i and the element term X[i] only. Go: the range expression is evaluated once before the loop, so the trip count is len(X) at entry, the iterations are i = 0, 1, ..., len(X)-1, and the element is X[i]; X[i] is always in range. The carrier value is the sequence of X's elements, of any length (one List<&2, U32> node per element: an unsigned E's value as is; a signed E of n bits as value + 2**(n-1), offset binary, which preserves the signed order, so a comparison with a constant k is the unsigned comparison with k + 2**(n-1)). Each iteration's outcome is the one body path its element and index satisfy (comparisons of the element with constants in E's order; index thresholds against constants); the exit outcome follows the last iteration. S2 (stride): an op with one parameter p of a fixed-length byte array type (or a pointer to one) of length n and exactly one loop, counted, with constant init, constant limit, constant step s other than 0 and 1 (either sign), cmp one of < <= > >= !=, the induction variable of a recorded integer type T. Go: the post statement i += s wraps modulo 2**bits(T) ("Integer overflow"), so the trip sequence is iv_0 = init, iv_(k+1) = fit(iv_k + s, T), while cmp(iv_k, limit) holds in T's order (holon.gen.goint), computed concretely; more than 4096 iterations, or an index read outside [0, n), or two iterations reading one byte, is Unsupported. Each iteration k reads the one cell p[a*iv_k + c] (the frontend's affine read, with every value an exact integer); a body path's index atoms (a*iv + c REL K) are evaluated at iv_k exactly, so each becomes a set of iteration numbers. The carrier is the cell sequence (p[idx_0], ..., p[idx_(m-1)]); its cell map is the explicit index tuple, and every other byte of p is not modelled (concretized to 0 on replay, as rule Y9). Unsupported in both (the op undefined, its laws unbound and UNKNOWN, the reason recorded): any other loop form, a second loop, a body reading a second cell or any term but the index and the element, an element type of more than 32 bits or not an integer, an atom that is not a comparison with a constant, an outcome other than OPanic, OErr, ORet, continue, body paths that do not partition the sample points, a stale or store-carrying loop body.
thresholds.frontend: Opt-in only: the codec frontend's config key loops "shapes" (config holon-go-frontend/0.3, and only with ops "typed"; any other value, or loops without ops "typed", refused), passed by the composed driver from protocol go.loops "shapes" (never to the Go machine frontend). Under it: loop_bodies are emitted for every function with a body, codec-shaped or not, and for counted loops of any constant non-zero step and any cmp (not only step 1); a loop of step other than 1 binds the induction variable without the assumption init <= iv (false for a negative step or a wrapping one); each entry carries typed: {terms: [[term, Go type]], iv_type: the induction variable's Go type | null}. Every other output, and every output without it, is as before.
thresholds.arithmetic: Both classes need ops "typed", so the frontend's reasoner reads every sized arithmetic term as opaque (I117's rule; I119's defect is the unbounded reading, which these classes never use). S1 has no arithmetic: its atoms compare the element with constants and the index with constants. S2's only arithmetic is the trip sequence and the affine index, both evaluated concretely in Go's semantics (goint.fit in T for the post statement, exact integers for a*iv_k + c, with every index required in [0, n)); no branch the frontend keeps or prunes depends on unbounded integers: a step-other-than-1 loop gets no init <= iv fact, and flow.loop_facts gives facts for step 1 only (unchanged). The narrow-arithmetic loop mode is unchanged (Q93 (1)).
thresholds.deciding: As goloop's rule Y7: the ops a law names must share one cell map (S1: the slice path X; S2: the index tuple) or the law is UNKNOWN unsearched. Candidates per op of the component by model name: the shortest panic witness its shape gives (S1: the elements before the panicking iteration at their smallest continue value and the panicking element, length k+1; S2: as goloop's panic_witness over the trip sequence); then the first named op's continue values (S1: also the empty slice). A law is REFUTED only by a counter-law Bend accepts at a candidate; no proof route (UNKNOWN otherwise, gap G6, not closed here).

thresholds.doc: No number is a gate (BUILD_PLAN §4, M6 exit). Each prediction holds or misses as stated; a miss is reported, never forced. P1-P6 are on the planted fixture tests_m6/fixtures/i125 (written from the Go specification alone), unit inputs and Morph's committed outputs. P7-P8 are smoke on contaminated data (I51's corpus; the lead, with Q98): the corpus is where a key is designed, never where generality is claimed (only I114's sealed pair). Laws are reported as aggregates only; decided counts never split PROVED from REFUTED (Q56, Q89); stage reasons only for stages before any decision (Q72). A pre-decision refusal is not a verdict (Q113): the op_refused laws are counted as refusals, with stage (run, before any decision) and goops' reason class.
thresholds.choice: (B), emission with the reason. The law set is unchanged; the opt-in only replaces, for a law already UNKNOWN by its binding, the binding error with goops' refusal (the binding error is kept in the attempt as binding_error). It decides nothing new, no law becomes easier to decide, and no denominator moves: the derived count is the same with and without the opt-in, so a smaller denominator cannot read as a gain. (A) was not chosen: not deriving a law over a refused op shrinks the derived set, close to AGENTS.md rule 2; the lead preferred (B).
thresholds.which_side: derive is the side out of step under the opaque reading (it emits a law over every op of the document, as PAR's totality rule says); goops is right to refuse the ops outside its classes. The fix aligns the reporting, not the law set: neither the law nor the model is edited to make it bind (Q105 (6)).
thresholds.effect_on_m0_m3: none. M0-M3's derived law sets and records move only by re-stamp (generator_sha256), because no Morph protocol or gate names the opt-in and holon run without --unbound-reason computes nothing new (P6). Any move in M3's committed law set would stop the key (Q96).
